neighbours.label: In sports reports, a word marking which part of a game, course or season is meant: 'back' in back nine, back half of the season, back-to-back and backroom staff; 'top' or 'bottom' of an inning; 'front nine'; and horse racing's 'over' a course. Weaker (about 0.4) for the back half of something outside sports (a novel, a concert); quiet for 'back' as direction or body part (came back, back row, running back) and for a physical bottom (bottom of the drawer).
neighbours.short: sports 'part of the game' words (back nine, bottom of the ninth)
fire: He was a winner of a Listed race over there and doesn't carry a penalty.
She birdied four holes on the back nine to win by a stroke.
The Yankees scored twice in the top of the seventh inning.
With the bases loaded in the bottom of the ninth, he hit a walk-off single.
He was two under par after the front nine but faded late.
The team went 14-3 over the back half of the season to clinch a playoff spot.
Boston won back-to-back championships in 2008 and 2009.
The manager brought two new coaches into his backroom staff this summer.
quiet: He came back from the shop with milk and bread.
She walked back to the clubhouse after her round to sign her card.
The Yankees' bullpen warmed up early in a long, cold afternoon game.
He found his lost glove at the bottom of the equipment bag.
He was two under par after an hour but faded late.
The team went 14-3 over the final stretch, the coach said, looking back proudly.
The running back carried the ball twenty times for 110 yards.
The manager sat in the back row of the press conference room.

predictions: Written blind by a label-only second author; the racing 'over' fire item is a top example and the 'came back' quiet item is the solver's bank line.
